description.narrative:
Rationale: - Increasing awareness of the impact of climate change and concern for the health of the Mekong and its tributaries - Recognising that women are disproportionately affected by climate change, play a crucial role in adaptation and mitigation and are also key in household and community water resource management - Building upon Oxfam’s inclusive approach, presence, partnerships (including with women’s rights organisations, people living with disability, CSO networks, the private sector and academia/research institutions) and programs across the Mekong Region including in Community Based Natural Resource Management (CBNRM) and Disaster Risk Management (Oxfam’s Strategy for Resilience in Asia | Oxfam International); expertise in transboundary water governance in the Mekong (Mekong Water Governance | Oxfam in Asia) and South Asia (Water Governance in the Transboundary Rivers of South Asia (TROSA) | Oxfam in Asia); experience in inclusive use of digital technology (see https://www.wgcan.org/EarlyWarningSystem.aspx); and access to data including current research on the Lancang-Mekong Cooperation Water Resources Sharing Platform (available in June 21) and a concept developed with E Water on Water Data Justice in the Mekong (in June 2019). - Capitalising on increased data access from water resource ministries, the LMC/MRC and new sources (eg the Mekong Dam Monitor Stimson Center) to ensure this data is utilised at local levels.
Concept: - Utilise river flow and satellite data sources to deliver real time information via a smart phone enabled platform linked to existing community – local Government structures (for example https://www.youtube.com/watch?app=desktop<(>&<)>v=x6BK9rfFgUE<(>&<)>feature=youtu.be) - Data to support short and medium term actions to address flood and storm events, drought and other weather-related hazards - Inclusive approaches to ensure access to women, men, youth, ethnic minorities/indigenous groups and people living with disability - Continued focus on increasing women’s knowledge of and leadership in sustainable resource management and DRM at thehousehold and community level in policies and practice - Access to improved and curated river flow and other meteorological data will be combined with support to community and local government CBNRM/DRM structures to utilise this data to enhance community resilience and women’s leadership in key locations along the Mekong and its tributaries - Additional activities to raise public awareness of the state of the Mekong River through targeted public awareness campaigns (main stream and social media) and community driven initiatives to address environmental and water quality issues such as river water quality monitoring (eg community water quality monitoring in the Mekong Delta supportedunder IP1) and youth focused river clean-ups (see https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ONsXmub8B-Q).

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam has had a presence in Lao PDR for longer than most INGOs, with both Oxfam in Belgium (OBE) and Oxfam Australia (OAU) beginning programming and establishing offices in the late 1980s. Oxfam’s vision is of a Laos in which all citizens – particularlywomen, the marginalised and discriminated groups – are able to claim their right to access opportunities and resources so as to overcome all forms of poverty and injustice.
Since 2015, the work of Oxfam in the country is governed by the Oxfam Country Strategy (2015-2019).We seek transformative changes in policies, practices and beliefs in ways that fundamentally improve the lives of poor and marginalised women and men, and ensure that all citizens have the same opportunities to enjoy their rights. Todo so, Oxfam focuses its work on four Domains of Change: Citizen Participation and Civil Society Development, Gender Justice, Resilient Communities and Sustainable Development, and Responsible Investment.
For this project, Oxfam in Laos will support theexpansion of the influencing work and public campaign on advocating for more inclusive social protection and access to social protection of the most marginalized workers. National public events will be organised, such Eliminate Violence Against Women Day(EVAW), and digital platforms will be used to socialize the information, and stir discussion and dialogue among rights holders, government stakeholders and policy makers. The campaigns will be implemented nationwide and in the provinces where Oxfam in Laos works. Target groups include marginalized workers, youth,women, CSOs as well as government stakeholders.
